think.q: Why is the saxophone in the Woodwinds family, even though it is made of shiny metal?
opts: Because it uses a reed, and you blow into it
think.why: The family depends on HOW the sound is made, not what it is made of. The saxophone uses a reed, just like a clarinet.

think.q: Why does a big tuba sound low, and a small flute sound high?
opts: Big instruments vibrate slowly, so they sound low
think.why: Bigger instruments have longer tubes or strings. They vibrate more slowly, and slow vibrations make low sounds. Small instruments vibrate fast and sound high.

think.q: How many parts (syllables) does the word vi-o-lin have?
think.why: Vi - o - lin. Clap it: three claps, three parts!

think.q: Why are the black keys in groups of 2 and 3?
opts: So we can find notes quickly, like landmarks
To make the piano look pretty
Because the black paint ran out
think.why: Without the groups, every key would look the same. The 2s and 3s are like signposts on the keyboard.

think.q: On the piano, you move your hand to the RIGHT. What happens to the sound?
think.why: Right means higher, left means lower. Every piano in the world works this way.

think.q: Which letter comes after G in the musical alphabet?
think.why: Music uses only A to G, so after G we start again at A.

think.q: You are on stone E, going forward. Which stone comes next?
think.why: Forward is A, B, C, D, E, F, G. After E comes F.

think.q: Going backward, which letter comes after C?
think.why: Backward is G, F, E, D, C, B, A. So after C comes B.

think.q: Which line does the treble clef curl around?
think.why: The treble clef starts on line 2 and curls around it. That is why line 2 is called G.

think.q: Where does the big dot of the bass clef go?
think.why: The bass clef is the F clef. It starts with a big dot on line 4, and its two little dots sit either side of that line, so line 4 is F.

think.q: How many quarter notes fill one 4-beat measure?
think.why: Each quarter note is 1 beat, so 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4.

think.q: How many beats does a half note last?
think.why: A half note is half of a whole note. Half of 4 is 2.

think.q: Quarter (1) + Half (2) = ?
think.why: 1 + 2 = 3. That is the same as one dotted half note!

think.q: A dotted half note lasts how many beats?
think.why: Half note = 2. The dot adds half of 2, which is 1. So 2 + 1 = 3.

think.q: Which line of the staff is line 1?
think.why: We always count the staff lines from the bottom up, so line 1 is the bottom line.

think.q: A note with a line going through its middle is a…
think.why: If the line goes through the middle, it is a line note. If it sits between lines, it is a space note.

think.q: To find A quickly, which landmark should you start from?
opts: F, because F, G, A is only 2 steps
think.why: From F it is F, G, A: 2 steps. From C it would be 5 steps. Closest landmark wins!

think.q: Which staff is on top in the grand staff?
think.why: Treble (high notes) is on top, bass (low notes) is below. High on the page, high in sound.

think.q: Middle C sits…
opts: On a small line below the treble staff
think.why: Middle C has its own little extra line, called a ledger line, just below the treble staff.

think.q: A lullaby should be…
think.why: A slow tempo and a soft volume help a baby relax and fall asleep.

think.q: In the treble clef, what does the word F-A-C-E spell?
think.why: The four treble spaces, from bottom to top, are F, A, C, E. They spell FACE!

think.q: All Cows Eat Grass helps you remember…
think.why: The bass spaces from bottom to top are A, C, E, G.

think.q: What is the best way to get better at music?
opts: One very long practice once a month
think.why: Short, regular practice helps your brain and fingers remember. Ten minutes every day is better than hours once a month.
